questions.stem: In the context of AWS, what best describes a compute resource?

options.text: The network bandwidth allocated to move data between services
The durable storage used to retain data after a task completes
The identity and access controls that authorize a workload
The processing power an application needs to carry out computational tasks through a series of instructions

explanation.correct: Compute resources are the processing power required by applications and systems to carry out computational tasks via a series of instructions.

distractors.A: Network bandwidth concerns data movement, not the processing power that executes instructions.
distractors.B: Durable storage retains data; it is not the processing power that carries out tasks.
distractors.C: Identity and access controls authorize workloads; they do not perform computation.

questions.stem: Which TWO common server components is compute most closely related to?

explanation.correct: Compute is closely related to CPUs and RAM — the processing and memory components that execute instructions.

distractors.A: Object storage holds data; it is not a processing component associated with compute.
distractors.C: DNS resolvers translate names to addresses and are unrelated to raw compute.
distractors.E: Load balancers distribute traffic and are not core compute components like CPUs or RAM.

questions.stem: Why is a physical server in a data center considered a compute resource?

options.text: Because it stores backups of application data
Because it provides a public IP address to applications
Because it has multiple CPUs and many gigabytes of RAM to process instructions from the OS and applications
Because it encrypts data at rest automatically

explanation.correct: A physical server qualifies as a compute resource because it has multiple CPUs and many gigabytes of RAM used to process instructions from the operating system and applications.

distractors.A: Storing backups is a storage function, not what defines the server as a compute resource.
distractors.B: Providing a public IP is a networking concern, not the reason it is compute.
distractors.D: Encrypting data at rest is a storage/security feature, unrelated to being a compute resource.

questions.stem: What does an Amazon EC2 instance represent?

explanation.correct: EC2 instances are virtual servers that provide compute capacity.

distractors.B: A managed relational database is a database service, not what an EC2 instance is.
distractors.C: Serverless functions describe Lambda, not EC2 instances.
distractors.D: A container image registry describes ECR, not an EC2 instance.

questions.stem: Which characteristic best describes how compute is consumed by an AWS Lambda function?

options.text: It runs continuously for months or years processing billions of instructions
It reserves a fixed pool of virtual servers for the account indefinitely
It uses a small amount of compute for a very short time in response to an event, then relinquishes it
It requires manually provisioning CPUs and RAM before each execution

explanation.correct: A Lambda function may use only a few milliseconds of compute to run code in response to an event, then relinquish that compute power.

distractors.A: Continuous, long-running processing of billions of instructions describes the EC2 end of the scale, not Lambda.
distractors.B: Lambda does not reserve a fixed indefinite pool of servers; it is serverless and event-driven.
distractors.D: Lambda does not require manually provisioning CPUs and RAM before each run; compute is provided on demand.

questions.stem: Which example reflects the long-running end of the AWS compute duration scale?

options.text: A couple of lines of Python executed in a few milliseconds
Hundreds of EC2 instances used continuously for months or years
A single event triggering a brief function invocation
A one-time query that returns immediately

explanation.correct: Using hundreds of EC2 instances continuously for months or years to process billions of instructions represents the long-running end of the compute scale.

distractors.A: A few milliseconds of Python execution is the short-lived, serverless end of the scale.
distractors.C: A brief event-triggered invocation is characteristic of short-lived Lambda compute.
distractors.D: A one-time immediate query is not an example of sustained long-running compute.

questions.stem: Which THREE of the following are core AWS compute services (as opposed to container services) introduced in this overview?

explanation.correct: EC2, AWS Batch, and AWS Lambda are core compute services in this overview; SAM is the fourth core compute item.

distractors.B: Amazon ECR (Elastic Container Registry) is a container service, not a core compute service.
distractors.D: Amazon EKS (Elastic Kubernetes Service) is a container service, not a core compute service.
distractors.F: Amazon ECS (Elastic Container Service) is a container service, not a core compute service.

questions.stem: Which THREE services are the AWS container services covered in this overview?

explanation.correct: The AWS container services in this overview are Amazon ECS, Amazon ECR, and Amazon EKS.

distractors.A: AWS Lambda is a core compute service, not a container service.
distractors.C: AWS Batch is a core compute service, not a container service.
distractors.E: AWS SAM (Serverless Application Model) is a core compute item, not a container service.

questions.stem: What does the acronym EC2 stand for?

explanation.correct: EC2 stands for Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud.

distractors.A: "Elastic Container Cloud" is not the expansion of EC2; container services are ECS/ECR/EKS.

questions.stem: What does the acronym ECR stand for?

explanation.correct: ECR stands for Amazon Elastic Container Registry.

distractors.A: ECR is not "Elastic Compute Registry"; it is a container registry, not compute.

questions.stem: Which container service's name reflects that it orchestrates Kubernetes?

explanation.correct: Amazon EKS is the Elastic Kubernetes Service, whose name reflects Kubernetes orchestration.

distractors.A: ECS is the Elastic Container Service and does not carry the Kubernetes name.
distractors.C: ECR is the Elastic Container Registry, used for images, not Kubernetes orchestration.
distractors.D: AWS Batch is a core compute service and is not a Kubernetes service.

questions.stem: Select TWO ways in which compute resources can vary when consumed in AWS.

options.text: By requiring the same fixed duration for every workload
In the length of time they are used
By being available only in a single performance option
By being limited to exactly one service category

explanation.correct: Compute can be consumed in different quantities and for different lengths of time, across a range of categories with varied performance options.

distractors.B: Duration is not fixed; workloads range from milliseconds to years.
distractors.D: Compute offers a variety of performance options, not a single one.
distractors.E: Compute spans a wide range of categories, not just one.

questions.stem: What does AWS SAM stand for?

explanation.correct: AWS SAM stands for the AWS Serverless Application Model.

distractors.D: SAM is the Serverless Application Model, not "Serverless Availability Model".

questions.scenario: A data engineering team is deciding how much compute to allocate for an upcoming workload. Some jobs will run continuously for long periods, while others are tiny and event-triggered. Leadership asks what should ultimately drive the choice of compute resources.
questions.stem: What should ultimately determine which AWS compute resources the team uses?

options.text: The alphabetical order of the service names
Always choosing the service with the most CPUs
Whichever service was released most recently

explanation.correct: The compute resources used in AWS ultimately depend on the organization's overall business requirements.

distractors.A: Service naming order has no bearing on the appropriate compute choice.
distractors.C: Maximizing CPUs is not the deciding factor; requirements drive the choice.
distractors.D: Release recency does not determine which compute is appropriate.

questions.scenario: An application must respond to individual events by running a couple of lines of Python for only a few milliseconds at a time, and it should not hold onto compute capacity when idle. The team wants to avoid running and paying for long-lived virtual servers for this task.
questions.stem: Which compute approach fits this event-driven, short-lived requirement best?

options.text: Running hundreds of EC2 virtual servers continuously
A serverless AWS Lambda function invoked in response to the event
Provisioning a dedicated physical server in a data center
Keeping a fixed fleet of EC2 instances running for months

explanation.correct: A serverless AWS Lambda function runs briefly in response to an event and relinquishes compute afterward, matching the short-lived, event-driven need.

distractors.A: Running EC2 servers continuously is the long-running model, the opposite of this requirement.
distractors.C: A dedicated physical server holds compute indefinitely and does not match a brief, event-driven task.
distractors.D: A fixed fleet running for months is long-lived compute, not the short-lived approach described.
